correctness.rationale: The claim is an exact finite 12-edge identity; direct enumeration tests all 4096 possible orientations and all 144 covariance entries, while an independent multivariate coefficient DP produces the same exact 38 and 144 moments. A rational Laplacian pseudoinverse supplies the projection; a rank-one spectral decomposition yields eigenvalues 0 (5), 32/19 (6), 36/19 (1). The five-vertex K5 baseline is separately enumerated. Both packaged Python scripts were executed successfully. No numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: The exact first-order Walsh frame gives sharp stable recovery bounds for the canonical smallest noncomplete simple four-valent ice graph. It is a motivated first-order non-tightness boundary after K5, not a renamed standard covariance calculation: there is a geometrically distinguished one-dimensional circulation and an exact anisotropy gap. This explicit constrained-spin benchmark may test approximations using scalar cycle projections, without claiming a general theorem for larger graphs.
